THE ANTI-AGING CHALLENGE: Why, What & How Why Do I Really Care About This? By Cordell M. Andersen

Strangely I have met a few people in the twilight of their life that don't really care very much about living too much more. Maybe it's just getting too hard for them, but more glaring is that they sadly don't have as part of their lives anything that is engaging and stimulating with life seemingly having lost its purpose. Therein we see right off our first secrets of "longevity" highlighted above. Others to the contrary are horrified with the thought of dying, maybe because what awaits them is too much of a mystery, or in some cases, because they aren't too confident that it will be pleasurable--rather they fear some kind of punishment awaits them and would just as soon put it off as long as possible. I recall one old fellow who early in my marriage we had to care for, who was so frightened of death that when it seemed imminent, he refused to go to bed for fear that he wouldn't wake up, so insisted on sitting up in his sofa chair for days at a time struggling to keep awake--which of course finally had him passing on quicker than normal! His way of trying to prolong his life was the opposite of what he needed. THE DECEPTION OF YOUTHFULL INVINCIBILITY! On the other hand many of the youth of today make the mistake of thinking they are invincible even doing things they know aren't good for them, but they like instant gratification, convinced that later on they can modify their behavior in time to avoid serious consequences--but apparently this approach is dangerous as my younger kids all say that they don't have any friends who have not contemplated suicide! That's scary, indicating something crucial is missing from their lives. As I grew up I was lucky as "suicide" never crossed my mind. I believe it was because personal faith was a dominant part of my life since childhood, but also because I came to have some deep seated interests that I looked forward to….so I always wanted to live. But, when 16 I didn't pay attention to certain warnings, and now 65 years later am suffering some hellish burning, due to a very difficult topical chemo treatment on my skin to combat the mistakes that started in my youth when exposed to too much intense sunlight without any protection. For the good of young people I'd better confess here one more of my youthful idiocies that is now causing me fits and usually blamed on old age--but it started when young! It wasn't just me, as I don't recall anybody talking about it back then, even when in the Army. I'm talking about hearing loss which started when I was 16 and today is so bad I'm on the verge of becoming

p. 617

a recluse, purposely keeping away from social situations, where I find myself just mimicking those around me, smiling when they smile, but not sure about what's funny! It started with my first big game rifle I purchased with savings working when 15 years old for a year from 5-7 AM every day cleaning the vomit and debris from Ted's Bar in Albany, California. It was a Remington 30-06, purchased when we moved to Provo, Utah. Wow, how I loved my first rifle and used it everywhere, even for rabbit hunting using cheap armor piercing Army surplus ammo, and none of us guys had ever heard of ear protection.

Here I am with my beloved Remington 30-06 and the harvest of my first deer hunt, having also harvested the beginning of the destruction of my hearing system--due to NO EAR PROTECTION! My buddy is my little brother Howard Maybe it was just a youth thing of us only paying attention to what we were interested in. But, later in the Army, with lots of training with big bore rifles, and even hand grenades, I don't recall any ear protection either. Consequently my hearing has always been borderline-bad, and always with the constant ringing that seems perfectly normal for me! But now, coupled with advancing years, it has become incurable and the one body part that is extremely defective and the one thing that makes me feel "OLD!" Obamacare doesn't consider such worn out old guys my age worth investing in to provide the fix I need--hearing aids. So, youth, protect your hearing, and don't make the mistake of saying, "No problem, I'm no Daniel Boone type shooting big bore rifles!" Your problem, some say is approaching epidemic proportions, being your earphones with your gadgets turned to the highest volume capable of ruining your ears as much as a 30-o6 rifle with no ear protection! A family example: My brother, eight years younger than me, suffered horribly the effects of cigarette smoking, his first emergency when 52 years old and only given a 2% chance of surviving--HE WON! But, that "brush with death," rather than having him humbly seek real purpose in his life and changes in his behavior, had him feeling invincible so he didn't abandon what had almost killed him….but one night he LOST the fight, passing on when 20 years younger than my present age. The same for a younger sister who was always preaching her good

p. 618

health beliefs--that were almost all valid….but she secretly sneaked out often when no one was looking to have a smoke and a donut…. and she was suddenly gone too soon!

Interested In Hanging Around I obviously am one interested in hanging in there, as long as I can be active, be of some value to the world and not be a burden to anyone. What are my reasons for wanting to prolong my life? It's maybe selfish and unnecessary as I have lived a quite intense life, and at least tried very hard to accomplish my dreams. Maybe it's best I move over and make room for someone else. My life, usually treading in dangerous places on the edge of death, either chasing cattle rustlers in Guatemala's backcountry, living through a 30 year Guerrilla War, or fighting gangbangers in Guatemala City; or now in the U.S., backpacking in treacherous Uinta or Wastach mountain remote terrain.

THE POINT BEING: I don't fear death, and will even welcome it if I'm suddenly ambushed by it-- as I have done my darndest to be ready. Nevertheless I'd like to put it off some still as I feel my life has important purpose with fairly pressing needs, two primary ones being:

1. Half century of work among the Mayans in Guatemala: I feel I have to keep alive and healthy as long as possible to continue the life saving and life changing work among the Mayans-life changing for them and for me. It started in a sense when I was 16 years old when I had a soul awakening NDE…"near death experience," followed by a revelatory dream that night, and a year later experienced a spiritual conversion, all of which started with a bang my VISION QUEST. That eventually lead me to the Land of the Mayas. NOTE: This first point might be considered mute as on August 19, 2017 we celebrated our GOLDEN ANNIVERSARY, and retired the Guatemalan Foundation--50 years after having crossed the border into Guatemala to begin our Andersen Family Peace Corp effort to help the Mayans. Yet, if any prosperity comes my way, I will again dedicate what I have to that life saving purpose. Continuing with the point written back in 2015: I'm still involved. I would like to persist a little longer as there hasn't appeared on the scene someone interested and willing to continue

p. 619

the volunteer work with the GUATEMALAN FOUNDATION. I find it fascinating that a brush with death lead me to my life's mission. See details at: . http://www.guatemalanfoundation.org/ See also for full understanding: Part 1 "The VISION QUEST," at: http://www.cordellmandersen.com/p/autobiography-0-22-yrs.html

2. The High Uintas Wilderness Project: I'd also like to finish this project that I started in 2003 with the objectives of not only helping outdoor lovers enjoy it and similar areas more, but also sharing my experiences so they can do it safely while being inspired and blessed by what I call the VISIONS OF NATURE. Once again I notice that several brushes with death in this effort have also given me more resolve to finish what I started. For details, see: http://www.cordellmandersen.com/ & YouTube video: #8-2013 Open Your Eyes to THE VISIONS OF NATURE

The historical view actually shows that the 2nd was the first in 1952 at 16, when introduced to the High Uintas by my buddies Ted Packard, and Charlie Petersen, resulting in a lifelong "love affair" and a vow to explore, photograph and report on the then High Uintas Primitive Area, but now Utah's greatest Wilderness. That vow was just a few months prior to my awakening NDE that eventually led to the 1st on my list, the Mayans. Each have complimented the other, keeping me alive and healthy to be able to persist with both. The historical 1st, the Uintas, might just end up being the last….as both involve well understood elements of worthwhile danger--all in harmony with what I recently quoted at the end of a photo/essay on my website:

"DEATH BE NOT BORING... ....I've lived well. I've adventured widely. I will not die poorly." by Jonathan Dorn

"NEVER GIVE IN ..... EASILY!" by Winston Churchill with my modified added last word

NOW TO THE FIGHT: MEETING THE AGING CHALLENGE Most of us don't worry too much about it….until it's almost too late. However there are warning signs, sometimes early on that we should pay attention to, and once they are solved we should become more sensitive to other changes that we can deal with….if we want to live a long, active, and purposeful life.

My First "Red light warning" In my case, after getting through the first two phases of my life, and into the meat of the dream realization phase, came a red light warning of a life and death fight at hand. I had all my workers on the Valparaiso Plantation in Guatemala trained and I was reduced to doing office work. I had also in previous years gone through some very stressful situations that made things worse. I was about 40 at the time, and gradually my weight had increased 30 pounds. I didn't worry too much until an elderly visitor, Stanford Robinson, commented how "out of breath" I was when just walking up a few stairs, or a small hill. I was embarrassed and decided to check on my heart and was stunned noticing it stopped beating for 4 or 5 seconds, three or four times a minute. I didn't feel any pain, but it shocked me and I immediately started working on what I calculated were the causes and consequent solutions: Lose weight, and start exercising. I began jogging for the first time in my life since sports in my youth. I added daily pushups, and going out to work in our large vegetable plots, and every other day working in our forest

p. 620

areas with my chain saw, preparing to begin heavy duty chopping of firewood, as seen in Rocky IV,--me beating one of his techniques shown in the 1984 movie, by 7 years.. The first day I jogged about 1 km. or half a mile, and it just about killed me, but I persisted. At the same time I focused on a healthier diet…not a very scientific formula…just smaller portions using a small plate--that I never loaded a second time. By about two weeks I had lengthened the distance to 3 miles, and lost around 10 lbs. and my heart irregularity went away. I persisted with jogging, and working, adding to my regimen chopping fire wood from the trees I had fallen, splitting sections into kindling using a wedge and a heavy duty ax that was a sledge hammer on one end. None of this was an economic need, rather a physical matter of life or death, which also did wonders for my mental and spiritual health. Soon I was down to 150 pounds, my weight when 20 years old, and felt like a new man.

The Second "Red Light Warning" The next warning light started flashing when I was about 49 and I began having arthritis in my right hand, elbow, shoulder and in my "motorcycle knee," and "football ankle," all strangely on my right side. I couldn't even lift a quart bottle of soda pop with that right hand. I really started getting worried. It was in the middle of the Guerrilla War in Guatemala and I had to be strong, ready and able to fight or take flight depending on circumstances --and it did happen a few times. By then I was driving the long trip from Guatemala to Provo, Utah every 2 months, and over 10 years traveled half a million miles to keep family, business and projects going, but would stop at most Rest Areas in the U.S. to do my 60 pushups & sometimes jog a bit, and had one of those two spring exercise gadgets fixed to the right side of the cab to pull in different ways often with both arms (one at a time of course), as well as a 5 lb. barbell I would work with to keep awake and keep strong. This had Dr. Harris Done, of AYUDA Inc. once remarking, "You must be a weight lifter." But, one night at about 11:00 PM coming into southern Utah listening to KSL radio to keep me awake, I heard an interview with Dale Alexander, who I learned was known as "The Cod Father." He had an arthritis solution using Cod Liver oil. He claimed it had worked for him, and his 80 year old mother and many more. I was desperate and willing to try anything in spite of it being pretty nasty stuff to swallow.

The "Cod Father's" Treatment Works! Are you too weak to apply it and prefer being a cripple? So for the next 6 months I took two tablespoons full each morning, 30 minutes before breakfast, and two more in the afternoon, 30 minutes before dinner. At 6 months the pain totally went away. From then on I took a tablespoon full each morning for maintenance. The pain never returned, until 2 years later, in 1987 when I got sick after two straight days of snorkeling in our lake in Guatemala with a spear gun after tilapia and giant black bass. The mysterious sickness had some preparing for my burial, and the cod liver oil was forgotten for a month and all the pain returned. I got back to it QUICKLY!

p. 621

I was shocked, but not surprised, and immediately starting taking it again, circling on the calendar when I began, and at exactly 4 months this time, the pain went away and has never returned….except some when doing especially heavy duty backpacking in the High Uintas Wilderness, when I increase the maintenance dose from 2 gel caps up to 6 each morning, two more at night and sometimes more during the day when I feel a bit of pain coming on. I had always understood it was a matter of it lubricating the joints, and maybe there is some truth to that, but it is mainly due to cod liver oil being an anti-inflammatory agent. See: http://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/1999/mar/02/healthandwellbeing.health2 I have revealed this to many over the years who complained about joint pain, and in many cases I actually gave them the first bottle of cod liver oil, with the charge that they persist for the 6 months buying their own after the free bottle. Sadly it seems that human nature has us stopping if we can't get fairly quick results (the "instant gratification" mind set)--so they would give up on the oil and persist all their lives complaining and becoming cripples! What a sad disaster! I have also explained this treatment on my website and in a photo/essay about GEAR/SUPPLEMENTS, and give links where to get everything. Has it done any good?

Pay Attention & It Will Work….Ask, Mike Atkinson During the summer of 2013 I made a backpack up Little East Fork of Blacks Fork and made a YouTube Video you can find at: http://youtu.be/dyRAoXlkvCQ In it I report meeting Mike Atkinson and his family…….Mike on the right.

I introduced myself to Mike, and he….hesitated a bit, looking me over and said,

"Yes, I know you. I've seen your website. Me and my brother really paid attention to your treatment for arthritis using cod liver oil which really works!" PLAN TO BECOME A GUINEA PIG! Yet, I don't know of many willing to try it long enough and I will admit frustration with so many unwilling to do what works to bless their lives. Maybe there are already more than Mike and his brother, but with a sincere desire to motivate people to apply the system and not have to whine and complain any longer, I proposed last Fall, and maybe mentioned this on one of my posts,

p. 622

that once deer hunting was over I would convert myself into a guinea pig to demonstrate this effective treatment, that even doctors smile at and make no comment. I was going to create a YouTube video of the experiment, explaining in it what I explain above, and on a certain date circled on the calendar stopping totally taking cod liver oil, and report exactly when all the pain returned (for the first time in 28 years). Then circle the date on the calendar when beginning again…even sacrificing the easy-to-take gel caps and use a tablespoon and the real nasty liquid stuff. Then, hope that all of a sudden the pain would go away--again, and report on it to hopefully convince many to give it a try. But, when Jesse heard he became really concerned for my life. He's my son--a Marine with a tour in Iraq, whose experience with healthy living and keeping strong with the Bullet Proof Diet will be quoted later. He is such a believer in healthy oils and fats, and especially cod liver oil as an anti inflammatory for me that he really was afraid that not only the arthritis on my right side would return, but also other inflammation in my whole body that would have otherwise developed over all these year if I hadn't of been taking the oil! He was afraid it would be more than my body could withstand….and I'd be gone! So I chickened out and never did it. Maybe I'll still do it in that day when the main purposes for my life are pretty well achieved, and about the only thing I would have left is to FINALLY CONVINCE EVERYONE ABOUT THIS LIFE ENHANCING AND SAVING NUTRITIONAL SUPPLEMENT and TREATMENT.

STRESS & A Broken Heart!....Get Up & Do Something! Then in 1994, as a consequence of six years of stressful effort to save my marriage, my heart was damaged bringing on high blood pressure and an irregularity….this time stuttering all the time. I often have said about that period of my life that "I lost six of the best years of my life!" Just imagine if that could have been avoided, the 15-20 years people guess my age less than it is….would be 21-26 years less, or my nearly 80 years would then be guessed as between 54 and 58! To keep stress…a potent aging contributor from being worse, and even a killer, I eventually did before it was too late, two things: One, I was often on my knees exercising my faith in a loving Father in Heaven, and in a loving Savior who promised He would always be with us, and asked fervently for help as though I couldn't by myself do anything…….then…. Two, I got up, stopped feeling sorry for myself, and went to work with a passion, as though it was all up to me, increasing my daily jogging and just after my 58th birthday ran my first race: The International Half Marathon in Coban, Guatemala. That was when the Kenyans invaded Guatemala and began dominating the race…and in that first race I actually saw them…

p. 623

…… coming back when I was still grinding my way to the turn-around point. In that race I actually beat the young barefoot Indian girl, Erlinda Xol, who later would become Guatemala's champion. In that 1994 race, a first for both of us, she had collapsed 50 meters from the finish line and I beat her…about 30 minutes later, but beaten by the Kenyans by 54 minutes.!

Another Glitch…."Metatarsalitus"….Finding More Solutions That brought on another challenge diagnosed in Guatemala as "metatarsalitus," on the ball of my feet where I felt acute pain like stepping on a rock. A rheumatologist advised me to forget running and to stop dreaming about backpacking. But, I wasn't about to quit and began experimenting modifying my running shoes, and hiking (work) boots, and bought footgear 2 sizes larger as I added different combinations of inserts, plus added supplements, like Glucosamine/Chondroitan/MSM, and persisted doing the race for 14 consecutive years, towards the end of that stretch living back in Utah and in the midst of my High Uintas Wilderness Project.

A New Challenge: The High Uintas Wilderness Project… …Many.Glitches & Solutions That brings us up into the new century, when in 2003, now back in the U.S., in my 68th year I began my High Uintas Wilderness Project with a 27 day, no-resupply, backpack I called an expedition, following the spine of the Uintas east, zig-zagging north and south for 206 miles, beginning at the Highline Trailhead with 83 lbs. on my back and around my waist.

A mile or so from the trailhead I met writer, Phillip Fradkin, author of SAGE BRUSH COUNTRY. 222 He didn't think I would make it and mentioned that in the new edition of his book he was working on then, but by publication time he had learned I had made it and added a comment in his book.223

222

SAGEBRUSH COUNTRY: Land and the American West, by Phillip Fradkin, 2004 by Johnson Books, Boulder

223

See page 586-387 of UTAH'S ALPINE WONDERLAND: THE HIGH UINTAS MOUNTAINS by Cordell M. Andersen

p. 624

He didn't know I had trained for it on my farm in Guatemala hiking 4 miles around the hilly property 2-3 times a week carrying a 100 lb. bag of cement or fertilizer on my shoulders. So by 2003 I had discovered a few basic secrets and was able to cope with some of the normal effects of getting old. However, the truth was that on the first night of that "expedition," my motorcycle knee, from a 1976 accident in Guatemala, was hurting so bad I was on the verge of throwing in the towel. 224 But, not being able to sleep that night I read all night the book I had brought for the trip.

It was, IT'S NOT ABOUT THE BIKE: My Journey Back to Life, by Lance Armstrong. It was a life saver for me, in spite of what happened to him years later, so I'm eternally grateful to Lance….and I have said jokingly, "I'd use performance enhancing stuff too, if I could afford it!" Of course, as you will see I do use many legal supplements that have made possible me persisting. His struggle, so much greater than mine, inspired me to not give in, and I found a way to persist. Each night, to be able to sleep an hour at a time, I would maneuver in my tent on all fours and put the knee into a 1 quart pot of cold water for 10 minutes--that each time gave me 1 hour of painless rest, repeated all night, for 25 nights! Once I was able to actually use snow which was incredible. That experience led me to Winston Churchill's famous words,

"NEVER, NEVER, NEVER GIVE IN!" 224

See APPENDIX 3 , DETAILS OF MY ONGOING STRUGGLE TO SOLVE GLITCHES

p. 625

Those who know me are aware that Churchill's cry to arms has been my theme for the last 16 years, now in 2018, with 2,000+ miles of backpacking under my belt. It has not been an easy path. There have been many glitches--each requiring a fix, and I have learned a lot that I will now share with those of you who have read this far. Many of my problems should be of interest to most of you, who, sooner or later will likely have to deal with similar detours in your path, and hopefully my solutions will be of some help to a few.

Moments of hesitation for Forest Gump & Me I have been lucky, and very blessed, but you will notice that it hasn't come easy, several times having had my Forest Gump moment when he, after running around America for 3 years with a little following behind him, stopped, turned and for the first time was going to speak. Someone among his followers yelled out, "Quiet, he's going to say something!" They expected some prophetic utterance, but he just said,

I've had several of those moments when dealing with all the glitches, and getting older had sometimes too hard and no fun anymore. Yet, the stubborn streak in my had me making a bunch of COMEBACKS, until 2015 when I did this original writing. So, still no "GIVING IN," and on the verge in 2015 of quixotically launching myself into a big summer of backpacking in the High Uintas Wilderness, even with plans to get to and photograph some remote lakes I haven't ever heard anybody has reached….even one that seems to be the highest in the Uintas and the state-- which I have facetiously named "Little Andy Lake," the idea coming last year from my buddies on KSL Outdoors Radio that a lake be named after me. So I chose the highest, and most remote lake--one with no name, and not even deserving of a Division of Wildlife Resource number, and for sure doesn't have fish life, but it will have the nickname of a guy who in 2012 was resigning himself to being a cripple!

Giving Kids Credit….My First Complete Physical For a moment let's back up to 2003, and in the interest of full disclosure, give my kids credit for being concerned for their crazy old dad, and at least suggesting before that "expedition" in my 68th year that I get a complete physical for the first time in my life. However, I suspected that

p. 626

any doctor worth his salt would have told me not to do it….so I went ahead, did the expedition, and then went in for the physical exam with Dr. Daniel Tovey from Springville. That was about the last time I saw Dr. Tovey, as he sent me to an Oncologist, a Cardiologist, Dermatologist, Orthopedic & Sports Medicine surgeon, and eventually to a Radiologist, Endocrinologist, and other specialists. That began an almost annual visit at the hospital, during the winter season to have:….adjusted….. fixed….replaced….reconstructed…. and/or …removed body parts that were worn out and failing me. Thanks to Medicare I was able to stretch out the jerryrigging of my body until now in 2015 when all my assets, brought back from Guatemala in 2002, are finally gone--and I am blessed at the same time having finished raising as a Mr. Mom my last 5 children who all became independent in 2013, with me also becoming independent, living in my tiny CabinA, a 7' x 11' travel trailer with everything built into it for me to not be a burden to anyone. In it I'll be able to do my exploring/photography, finish managing the Guatemalan Foundation until August 2017 when it will be retired on celebrating its GOLDEN ANNIVERSARY, and then write the book. But, not to worry, everything has been fixed and/or supplements found that will have me blessed in 2015 with another great backpacking season in my 80th year, which rest assured I will share with all......of course recognizing that at any moment this dream could abruptly end.

NOTE: From here on I'll update everything to 2018 when I'm editing and adding visuals in preparation to insert this article into my book's Appendix.

The "JERRY-RIGGING" of my body to keep me from "GIVING IN!" Gratefully it will be very obvious, with the following list of medical interventions, with which I am incredibly blessed as without modern medicine I would have been most likely dead years ago, or at least been a cripple having accomplished very little or nothing. -2003: Cancerous thyroid removed -2003 & 2005: Radiation treatments -2003: Mohs surgery on two serious skin cancers -2003 to 2018: Many topical chemo skin treatments due to too much unprotected exposure in areas of intense solar radiation (West Utah Desert, Guatemala & High Uintas). -2004: The 2nd temporary arthroscopic surgery on the "motorcycle knee" The 1st was in 1976 when told "no more jogging or backpacking," but two weeks later my son David and me backpacked to the very top of the Henry Mountains bivouacking up there deer hunting when the root beer in our canteens froze and we almost died of thirst! -2004: 6 weeks after the knee surgery, on a late trip to Kings Peak, I became very sick, took antibiotics and other medications--laid there two days until beginning to take effect, then limping back towards the trailhead, had a heart attack, but with the help of the Lord survived and made it miraculously to the Trailhead the next day--heart irregularity gone. Protective measures then started on my heart and I began carrying

p. 627

every minute of every day a little Emergency pack with aspirin, and Nitro Glycerin…..almost never used. -2006: Completed 1,000 miles of backpacking, had a late season survival experience and first struggle with High Altitude Sickness, helicoptered out. -2007: Reconstruction of "football ankle" (injured in 1953), with tendon transplant and 3 screws holding it together -2008: Complete knee replacement surgery on "motorcycle knee" now titanium -2008 : DECLARED A CANCER FREE SURVIVOR -2009: Terminate reduction surgery on nasal passages to improve breathing. -2012: Back surgery for pinched nerve and crippling pain in my left "good leg!" -2013: Hip replacement surgery now with titanium hip on left side…resulting in…….. NO PAIN ANYWHERE IN MY BODY FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 30 YEARS! -2015: May 2015 Blood pressure consistently low & stopped taking medication -2016: Learned to manage High Altitude Sickness, got to Little Andy Lake, and reached goal of 2,000 miles of backpacking since 2003. -2017: April 2017, 2nd Back surgery for pinched nerve--fusing last vertebrae's

NOW TO THE ANTI-AGING SECRETS THAT BLESS MY LIFE--in addition to #1 COD LIVE OIL already covered At least they've worked pretty good for me--so far NOTE: The following post on my website deals with some of this, entitled: WHERE DO YOU GET SO MUCH ENERGY? http://www.cordellmandersen.com/2010/06/where-doyou-get-so-much-energy.html The human body is one incredible machine. This will be an attempt to simplify a very complicated matter--the function of the human body, with a few key items that seem to have worked pretty good…and have a few thinking I'm a lot younger than I am. They are:

1. WAR IN OUR BODY: Free Radicals vs Anti-Oxidants 2. HUMAN GROWTH HORMONE 3. DHEA HORMONE 4. TESTOSTERONE HORMONE 5. COLLAGEN 6. HYALURONIC ACID 7. IMMUNE SYSTEM 8. USE IT OR LOSE IT! Let's take them in order, simplifying as much as possible---quite easy for this old guy, but to have deeper understanding, best do your own homework researching each item.

p. 628

1. THE WAR RAGING IN OUR BODIES The aging process is influenced by what we may call a "WAR BETWEEN GOOD & EVIL" going on inside of our bodies. The "bad guys" are called "free radicals," being what we can describe as damaged molecules that freely wander around in our bodies seeking to complete their own incomplete selves by taking away from, and in the process, destroying the good and crucial life giving and preserving cells and systems in our bodies. These free radicals create a chain reaction that can spread and destroy quickly, if not stopped. This is a process called oxidation, sort of like what it sounds like--a process of breaking down, similar to rusting away an old car, or rotting a piece of wood, or fruit, like when a cut apple turns brown and rotting begins, or other foods turn rancid, etc.

Some of the sources of free radicals are:

X-rays and radiation, injuries and inflammation, exercise, cigarette smoking, environmental pollutants, pesticides and other chemicals (like in Guatemala, "Pentadine" used to preserve wood from rot and termites…this likely being what caused cancer in my thyroid), industrial solvents, certain drugs, etc. These free radicals damage biologically molecules leading to cell damage and shorten our life span with aging problems such as weakness, damaged immune system, wrinkles, and then the deathly problems, such as, cancer, heart disease, arthritis, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, stroke, and more. But, the war isn't one sided, as there are "good guys" to confront, stop, destroy the free radicals and create some balance in our bodies.. We call them:

ANTI-OXIDANTS--the "good guys" They basically take up the fight in our defense scavenging free radicals interacting with them and terminating the chain reactions before vital molecules are damaged. Thus they have a significant influence on aging, and positively influence our life-span. Some of them form the "first line of defense" preventing the formation of free radicals. Others form the "second line of defense" scavenging the free radicals to stop the chain reaction from ever starting. Some of them, like glutathione, ubiquinol (CoQ10), and uric acid are produced by the body's metabolism, but with old age one's metabolism slows down and produces less creating all the problems associated with aging. Others need to come from our diet, or from supplements, such as Vitamins A, C, B-carotene, and E--known as the most potent radical scavengers. One's diet should focus on foods rich in antioxidants, such as a wide variety of vegetables, fruits and nutritious weeds, such as purslane and dandelions. Especially strong antioxidants are berries, cherries, citrus, prunes and olives. You will notice as we proceed that almost all the recommendations in the other categories listed above and detailed below, are made up of many foods, herbs, vitamins and supplements that are potent antioxidants….the "good guys" we need more of in the fight. NOTE: For more info. go to PHARMACOGOSY REVIEW, "Free radicals, antioxidants and functional foods: Impact on human health" found at: http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3249911/ .-

2. HUMAN GROWN HORMONE--HGH This crucial hormone is produced by the pituitary gland. It fuels childhood growth, and helps maintain tissues and organs. Beginning in middle age the pituitary gland slowly reduces the

p. 629

amount produced, and with oncoming old age the secretion declines dramatically. The deficiency, as one ages normally, produces an increase in fat mass, a reduction of muscle mass, loss of bone density, degrading of heart health and the immune system. That is accompanied by decreased energy, impaired learning and memory, with a resultant loss in quality of life, and mental and emotional well-being. Could there be a worse scenario? All of that brings to mind the comedy movie, "GRUMPY OLD MEN" with Jack Lemmon & Walter Matthau, where we learn to laugh at ourselves as we get into that scene. THIS IS THE CRUX OF AGING! It seems a bit controversial what can be done about it, but I'll propose a few ideas, leaving again in your hands the chore of doing your own homework. Here I'm just trying to simplify, reducing the ideas to the basics, and telling you about my experience. There are very expensive injections under the skin, and there are crèmes and pills. options are very expensive and apparently not a sure bet.

Those

Then there are the options more available to most of us. They are even more controversial, nonetheless have worked quite dramatically for me. They are usually called HGH Stimulators, or Releasers, composed of animal protein, amino acids, and other substances that are promoted to naturally stimulate the body's own production of HGH. They claim to enhance the efficacy of sleep and/or exercise, and hopefully neutralize the awful results of deficiencies listed above. They are recommended to take prior to going to sleep at night, or before heavy duty exercise. I have a history of around 15-20 years taking one of these products. For quite a while it was one from Goldshield, called, Time Fighters--Anti-Aging Formula, costing about $1.00/day. You can learn about it at: http://www.herbals-unlimited.com/TimeFIGHTERS-Anti-Aging-Formula.htm

My experience: It was when I worked for 3 years at REAMS Supermarket in Springville, Utah from 2009 to 2012. I purposely got a part-time job to—yes, to make a little money, but more importantly to force me to exercise and keep me strong during the backpacking offseason. The job I was after, interestingly was done previously by one of my sons, and he told me, "You'll hate it as it's the worst job in the world!" I replied, that I had never had a job I was sorry for, and that I would find a way to love it. So I requested a job in which I would do around 8 miles a day, 4 days a week, and began having fun with it, calling myself a "shopping cart herder & bagger technician….maybe the oldest in the world!" I also became a sign hanging engineer & a toilet/restroom scientist. I began a whole new public relations program, literally jogging everywhere, especially to help the customers with their groceries, and soon became famous knowing around 400 customers by their names….with several of the ladies falling in love with me. APPENDIX 6 Giardia infection (giardiasis)227 Giardia infection is an intestinal infection marked by abdominal cramps, bloating, nausea and bouts of watery diarrhea. Giardia infection is caused by a microscopic parasite that is found worldwide, especially in areas with poor sanitation and unsafe water. Giardia infection (giardiasis) is one of the most common causes of waterborne disease in the United States. The parasites are found in backcountry streams and lakes but also in municipal water supplies, swimming pools, whirlpool spas and wells. Giardia infection can be transmitted through food and person-to-person contact. Giardia infections usually clear up within a few weeks. But you may have intestinal problems long after the parasites are gone. Several drugs are generally effective against giardia parasites, but not everyone responds to them. Prevention is your best defense. Symptoms Some people with giardia infection never develop signs or symptoms but still carry the parasite and can spread it to others through their stool. For those who do get sick, signs and symptoms usually appear one to three weeks after exposure and may include: 

Watery, sometimes foul-smelling diarrhea that may alternate with soft, greasy stools



Fatigue or malaise



Abdominal cramps and bloating



Gas or flatulence



Nausea



Weight loss Signs and symptoms of giardia infection may last two to six weeks, but in some people they last longer or recur. Causes Giardia parasites live in the intestines of people and animals. Before the microscopic parasites are passed in stool, they become encased within hard shells called cysts, which allows them to survive outside the intestines for months. Once inside a host, the cysts dissolve and the parasites are released. Infection occurs when you accidentally ingest the parasite cysts. This can occur by swallowing contaminated water, by eating contaminated food or through person-toperson contact.

227

https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/giardia-infection/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20372790

p. 651

Swallowing contaminated water The most common way to become infected with giardia is after swallowing contaminated water. Giardia parasites are found in lakes, ponds, rivers and streams worldwide, as well as in municipal water supplies, wells, cisterns, swimming pools, water parks and spas. Ground and surface water can become contaminated from agricultural runoff, wastewater discharge or animal feces. Children in diapers and people with diarrhea may accidentally contaminate pools and spas. Eating contaminated food Giardia parasites can be transmitted through food — either because food handlers with giardiasis don't wash their hands thoroughly or because raw produce is irrigated or washed with contaminated water. Because cooking food kills giardia, food is a less common source of infection than water is, especially in industrialized countries. Person-to-person contact You can contract giardiasis if your hands become contaminated with fecal matter — parents changing a child's diapers are especially at risk. So are child care workers and children in child care centers, where outbreaks are increasingly common. The giardia parasite can also spread through anal and oral sex. Risk factors The giardia parasite is a very common intestinal parasite. Although anyone can pick up giardia parasites, some people are especially at risk: 

Children. Giardia infection is far more common in children than it is in adults. Children are more likely to come in contact with feces, especially if they wear diapers, are toilet training or spend time in a child care center. People who live or work with small children also are at higher risk of developing giardia infection.



People without access to safe drinking water. Giardiasis is rampant wherever sanitation is inadequate or water isn't safe to drink. You're at risk if you travel to places where giardiasis is common, especially if you aren't careful about what you eat and drink. The risk is greatest in rural or wilderness areas.



People who have anal sex. Having anal sex without using a condom puts you at increased risk of giardia infection, as well as sexually transmitted infections. Complications Giardia infection is almost never fatal in industrialized countries, but it can cause lingering symptoms and serious complications, especially in infants and children. The most common complications include:



Dehydration. Often a result of severe diarrhea, dehydration occurs when the body doesn't have enough water to carry out its normal functions.



Failure to thrive. Chronic diarrhea from giardia infection can lead to malnutrition and harm children's physical and mental development.

p. 652



Lactose intolerance. Many people with giardia infection develop lactose intolerance — the inability to properly digest milk sugar. The problem may persist long after the infection has cleared. Prevention No drug or vaccine can prevent giardia infection. But commonsense precautions can go a long way toward reducing the chances that you'll become infected or spread the infection to others.



Wash your hands. This is the simplest and best way to prevent most kinds of infection. Wash your hands after using the toilet or changing diapers and before eating or preparing food. When soap and water aren't available, alcohol-based sanitizers are an option. However, alcohol-based sanitizers are not effective in destroying the cyst form of giardia that survives in the environment.



Purify wilderness water. Avoid drinking untreated water from shallow wells, lakes, rivers, springs, ponds and streams unless you filter it or boil it for at least 10 minutes at 158 F (70 C) first.



Keep your mouth closed. Try not to swallow water when swimming in pools, lakes or streams.



Use bottled water. When traveling to parts of the world where the water supply is likely to be unsafe, drink and brush your teeth with bottled water that you open yourself. Don't use ice, and avoid raw fruits and vegetables, even those you peel yourself. Treatment Children and adults who have giardia infection without symptoms usually don't need treatment unless they're likely to spread the parasites. Many people who do have problems often get better on their own in a few weeks. When signs and symptoms are severe or the infection persists, doctors usually treat giardiasis with medications such as:



Metronidazole (Flagyl). Metronidazole is the most commonly used antibiotic for giardia infection. Side effects may include nausea and a metallic taste in the mouth. Don't drink alcohol while taking this medication.



Tinidazole (Tindamax). Tinidazole works as well as metronidazole and has many of the same side effects, but it can be given in a single dose.



Nitazoxanide (Alinia). Because it comes in a liquid form, nitazoxanide may be easier for children to swallow. Side effects may include nausea, flatulence, yellow eyes and brightly colored yellow urine. There are no consistently recommended medications for giardiasis in pregnancy because of the potential for adverse drug effects to the baby. If your symptoms are mild, your doctor may recommend delaying treatment until after the first trimester. If treatment is necessary, discuss the best available treatment option with your doctor.

APPENDIX 7 NOTE: This article is from the REI website

How to Choose PLBs and Satellite Messengers

While deeply rewarding, backcountry adventures also entail risks that can occasionally prove life threatening—even for the most experienced outdoor enthusiasts. Technology has come to the rescue with: 



Personal locator beacons (PLBs): Available in the U.S. since 2003, these satellite-based handheld devices provide a powerful safety net for wilderness travelers. Satellite messengers: A more recent innovation, these handheld devices—such as those from SPOT and DeLorme—have evolved to offer additional backcountry communication options.

Though both are portable transmitters, personal locator beacons and satellite messengers have some important distinctions. This article covers the basics of each .

Personal Locator Beacons Personal locator beacons are high-powered (typically, 5 watts) devices designed primarily to send out a personalized emergency distress signal. They generally require an open view of the sky to transmit successfully. PLBs are the land-based equivalents of Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacons (EPIRBs), a technology that has been in use for decades in marine environments. Over the years, these devices are estimated to have saved more than 43,000 lives.

Important: A Personal Locator Beacon should be activated only in situations of grave and imminent danger, and only as a last resort when all means of self-rescue have been exhausted.

How a PLB Works

p. 654

No matter where you are in the world, when you activate a PLB, it transmits a powerful signal at 406 MHz (MegaHertz), an internationally recognized distress frequency monitored in the U.S. by NOAA (National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration), the AFRCC (Air Force Rescue Coordination Center) and the USCG (United States Coast Guard). The signal is sent to a network of American, Russian, Canadian and French weather and global navigation system satellites that are part of the COSPAS-SARSAT international satellite-based search and rescue system (SARSAT is an acronym for "Search and Rescue Satellite Aided Tracking"). COSPAS-SARSAT uses a constellation of satellites, known as MEOSAR (Medium Earth Orbit Search and Rescue), which allows for near instantaneous detection of the PLB signal and the ability to locate the PLB without GPS-encoded information anywhere in the world. After receiving your transmission, the satellites "fix" on your location using frequency of arrival (FOA) and time of arrival (TOA) methods, then relay your information to the AFRCC or the USCG depending on the location of your alert. If you use a GPScompatible PLB, it can deliver your GPS coordinates to search and rescue personnel through the satellite system. This information is passed on to local search and rescue authorities who will come to your assistance.

Personalized Signal Federal law requires that all PLBs be registered in the NOAA SARSAT (Search and Rescue Satellite Aided Tracking) database. Registering your device is free of charge and the data is protected and only shared with rescue forces when your PLB is activated. When you register, NOAA will link your essential personal information to a 15character code known as a Unique Identifying Number (UIN). When activated, the PLB transmits your UIN to the COSPAS-SARSAT satellites via electronic bursts. While the electronic bursts provide search-and-rescue units with your location, the UIN tells them personal information such as your name, address, phone number and any medical conditions you may have. You can register your device and update personal information at www.beaconregistration.noaa.gov .

Two Types of PLB Signals When activated, a PLB sends 2 signals: 406 MHz (which carries the UIN and GPS data to the satellites) and 121.5 MHz, a homing frequency. The 406 MHz signal from the satellite will get rescuers to within 5 kilometers of your position. Then search-and-rescue teams will use a tracking device to home in on the 121.5 MHz and the 406 MHz frequencies. GPS-compatible PLBs also deliver the GPS coordinates of your position (accurate to to within 500 meters) to search and rescue personnel through the satellite system. Note: REI carries only models with a GPS interface.

p. 655

Keep in mind that it's always a good idea to have a visual and/or audible distress signal such as a signal mirror, whistle or strobe light to help catch search and rescue's attention when they get close. Many PLBs include a built-in LED signal light for this purpose.

How Long Will a PLB Transmit? A PLB comes equipped with a long-lasting lithium battery. This battery remains dormant until you flip the switch to activate the PLB. By COSPAS-SARSAT regulations, a PLB must transmit for this amount of time:  

A class 1 heavy-duty battery must be able to transmit at -40°F (-40°C) for 24 hours. A class 2 battery must be able to transmit at -20°F (-28.9°C) for 24 hours. (Most PLBs for recreational use have a class 2 battery.)

Cold temperatures will shorten a battery's operating time, and the situations above represent worst-case scenarios. For example, at a temperature of 70°F, these batteries will operate for approximately twice as long as they will at very cold temperatures. REI currently carries PLB models from ACR Electronics. No Subscription Fees Unlike with satellite messengers, you do not have to pay any recurring fees in order to use a PLB.

Satellite Messengers228 Much like PLBs, satellite messengers are handheld transmitting devices that are useful in backcountry areas far from reliable cell phone coverage. These user-friendly devices allow you to communicate short text messages and/or your location coordinates with friends or family back home so you can report on your trip’s status or, in an emergency, send calls for help. While a handy tool for casual hikers and backpackers, satellite messengers transmit signals that are much less powerful than a PLB signal. They are not intended for serious mountaineering use. How a Satellite Messenger Works 228

See at the end of this article info on THE NEWEST SPOT 2-WAY SATELLITE TRACKER

p. 656

Satellite messengers are GPS-based devices that rely on either of 2 commercial satellite networks—Iridium or Globalstar—rather than the military network used by PLBs. Emergency calls using either network are routed to the privately run GEOS International Emergency Response Coordination Center headquartered near Houston, Texas. A subscription fee is required to use a satellite messenger. Each manufacturer offers a variety of usage plan options, usually including duration (yearly, seasonally or monthly) and GPS tracking frequency (with intervals ranging from hours down to a few minutes). What are the differences between the satellite networks?

Iridium:   

Used by DeLorme devices. Offers 100% planetary coverage via a 66-satellite network. Uses 2 ground-based gateways (rather than satellites) process and switch messages.

Globalstar:   

Used by SPOT devices. Covers most of Earth’s land masses (except polar regions and sub-Saharan Africa) via a 48-satellite network. Uses 24 ground-based gateways to process and switch messages.

Note: Satellite messenger devices are considerably less powerful than PLBs and virtually always require an open view of the sky to transmit successfully. Each satellite network has its share of fans and detractors relating to their ability to deliver messages 100% of the time. At this point, the jury is still out.

APPENDIX 8 - A photo album THE TIE HACKER MUSEUM & MONUMENT in Dubois, Wyoming Dubois, Wyoming is located on the eastern slope of the Wind River Mountains, 277 miles north of Evanston, Wyoming.

The monument is found 17 miles northwest of Dubois dedicated in 1948

In downtown Dubois there are several museums, one to the Big Horn Sheep, and then to the TIE HACKERS which is a series of cabins in which the work and life of the tie hackers is explained and demonstrated.

p. 661

(photos / maps — no text on this page)

Flumes & river runs to get the ties to civilization

p. 663

(photos / maps — no text on this page)

p. 664

The tie hacker work & life as told in the museum is from the 1912 to 1936 period. From the early 1867 to 1880 period there is little documentation, and no personal journals and, as explained in my reports, many of the remains of that period are almost all gone, rotted away. In some of the writings about the modern 1912- 1036 period, mention is made of them listening to KSL radio on radios like we see below.

Some cabins and photographs depict the living conditions of single tie hacks, and families of tie hackers, showing the kitchens, the one room schools, saddle & repair shops, Forest Service office that supervised their work, etc. In the early period there was no Forest Service yet, and consequently few if any records.

For anyone interested in our western history, a visit to Dubois would be more than worthwhile. ****************************************

APPENDIX 10 The LEGEND OF SMALLFOOT & His Discovery by An Open minded YETI My quite mystical experience up Little East Fork of Blacks Fork--that not only gave insight into the legend of BIG FOOT, or SASQUATCH, but introduced LITTLE FOOT-even with the human ability to ride a horse. I ended my report of that trip meeting Mike Atkinson, and inserted a picture of us--calling me also Little Foot. As I did that I could never have guessed how much that was in harmony with a new chapter in the Legend. As I inserted the experience in the book, I began hearing of an animated movie entitled, SMALLFOOT,232 so felt I could leave no stone unturned in promoting better understanding--so, off I went to do research at the movie theater, to see:

I learned that the YETI version of the Big Foot legend, found in the Himalayas, involved a whole community of them who lived on the snowy peaks above the clouds. They were taught "truths" recorded in stones, one being that there was nothing below the clouds, and that the idea of tiny human creatures was a myth. But all of a sudden a plane crashed and one of the Yeti, Migo, actually saw what he called a Small Foot, and for testifying of it was banished from the community.

APPENDIX 11 THE CENTRAL UTAH PROJECT Developing Utah’s share of Uinta Mountain water from the Colorado River Drainage

As one leaves the Wasatch Front—Salt Lake City, or Provo--to drive to the High Uintas, it’s impossible to miss the reservoirs in the canyons. From Provo to Heber, we drive by Deer Creek Reservoir on the Provo River. From Salt Lake to Kamas, you drive by large Jordanelle Reservoir, also on the Provo River, seen below from the south side along the highway from Heber to Francis.

If coming through Coalville, you pass by Echo Reservoir, and then from Coalville to Oakley and then Kamas, drive by Rockport Reservoir, both of them on the Weber River. If you are heading from the Wasatch Front to the Uinta Basin and the Uinta’s South Slope, you pass by very large Strawberry Reservoir, enlarged with water from the Central Utah Project’s system of sending water from the Uinta’s South Slope, and then just before getting to Duchesne, you pass by Starvation Reservoir, in part with water from the Duchesne River. Other reservoirs are in the Vernal area of the Uintas like Steinaker Reservoir, and we have already visited the……..

……on Rock Creek from which water is taken through an underground aqueduct to the Current Creek Reservoir, and from there on to Strawberry. As mentioned previously, 90% of Utah’s water comes from the Uinta Mountains, and has to be managed properly, THE CENTRAL UTAH PROJECT, the prime player in that challenge. Learn more about this incredible system on the internet, at: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Utah_Project, and https://www.mitigationcommission.gov/aboutus/aboutus_cup.html and others.

APPENDIX 15 NEW INFORMATION ABOUT High Altitude Sickness Of THE BEST BACKPACKER….. p. 215

It all started here at Tungsten Lake in the upper Garfield Basin, South Slope

INTRODUCTION: Prior to publication I ran by Bob the description of his struggle with what for years was interpreted as HIGH ALTITUDE SICKNESS—HAS. He replied as follows: My heart rate was actually 200+, not 120+ as me and my brother reported to you in 2012. And, while for years I really thought the problem was one of HAS, I've slowly changed my mind. Last spring, it happened again, while I was on a morning 10k run with friends. Lightheadedness, couldn't keep running, pulse of 200+. I wound up in the cardiac emergency room in the Swedish Hospital where they monitored the same symptoms I had experienced in the Uintas. That afternoon, my heart rate subsided and I was released the next morning after undergoing more tests. I was diagnosed with "atrial flutter," a condition similar to the more common "afib" or "atrial fibrillation". To prevent re-occurrences, in May I underwent a cardiac catheter ablation where they run a wire up your femoral artery and into your heart where they can stimulate the "flutter". Then they map it and with pinpoint application of heat destroy the nerve cells inside the right atrium of my heart that were firing incorrectly. Amazing procedure, but I'm pronounced "cured" and have no reason to limit my physical activities in any manner. At least I hope so, because it hasn't happened since and I'm planning a summer of hiking.

Thanks, Bob for the update. It's great that you are pronounced ready to go again. But, going back to the 2012 experience--the fairly extreme drop in elevation caused a quite dramatic change in your state of health--similar to what is the case with many sufferers with HAS. Don't you think that High Altitude Sickness was also a part of what you experienced? Often life is more complicated than we would like it to be, similar to what I have experienced several times which has been a sort of domino effect when pushing myself too much after a surgery, the fatigue weakening my immune system and bringing on sickness, consequently making me vulnerable to High Altitude Sickness. Several of my survival experiences seem to follow that pattern, like in 2015 I attempted to get to Little Andy Lake by going up the Lake Atwood Trail, but when I got to the Chain Lakes area, I began feeling sick, so camped and noticed that night a fast pulse, and for the first time in 10 years my irregular heart beat had returned which had me taking seriously what was happening. I couldn't sleep experiencing shortness of breath--waking up every time I would dose off like suffocating. In the morning it had persisted so I packed up and headed carefully down and soon felt fine. The irregular heart beat hasn't returned and I have learned to manage my HAS using an Oximeter, taking it slow and easy and using Diamox. In 2016 I did a 6 day backpack up Henrys Fork, and finally made it to Little Andy Lake.

READER…..you judge, but BE CAREFUL!

p. 680

2018-2019 LAKES REVISIONS/UPDATING: All the pamphlets are outdated—many years ago, I therefore approached personnel from the DWR to get updated information. A meeting was set for November 2018 of the UAC—Utah Anglers Coalition and the DWR with the only agenda item “dedicated to [updating] the Uinta Mountain Lakes.” But in the end for whatever reasons it never happened.

p. 682

Consequently a meeting was arranged between me and knowledgeable DWR personnel on February 4, 2019. Two met with me at the DWR offices in Salt Lake City: Randy Oplinger, Sportfish Coordinator, and Matt McKell, Regional Biologist of the North Slope lakes working out of the Ogden office, plus via phone hookup, Garn Birchell, Regional Biologist of the South Slope lakes, from the Vernal DWR office. We had a 3 hour session reviewing all of the “experimental” and other changes with lakes of the Uintas over the past 34 years. In addition the DWR provided me with a link to all of their Stockings 237 of lakes and streams from 2002 to 2018, plus those ongoing in 2019. All of that information was used over a week of intensive effort to update the more than 630 lakes of the Uintas described in this book, making it the only publication to date with updated information—for 2018, and an important one scheduled for 2019 at Crater Lake plus a planned for restoration project for the Oweep, Ottoson, and Garfield Basins, and Fall Creek drainage. Since, I have been advised by Roger Wilson, who worked for many years with the DWR, and now Chairman of the Utah Anglers Coalition, that beginning in the summer of 2019 they will be working with the DWR to put together an updated management plan for the High Uintas. He feels that this will help the DWR manage better many of these remote lakes.

THIRTY-EIGHT YouTube Videos PRODUCED BY THE AUTHOR Go to the website for links: https://cordellmandersen.com/youtube-videos/ FROM THE FIRST--1000 MILE BACKPACK IN THE UINTAS in 2006, then FROM the MOST RECENT TO THE OLDEST ************************

THE 1000 MILE BACKPACK The SALT LAKE TRIBUNE, Oct. 4, 2011, called: "The grandfather of all Utah hiking slide shows." See APPENDIX 2 INTRODUCTION: This show represents a bit over 1,000 miles of backpacking in 4 summers–from 2003 to 2006. Some of those miles entail trips to certain areas several times in the constant quest of that “ perfect photograph,” or catching the “record breaking fish.” The Highline Trail was actually hiked twice in the 1,000 miles, the second time to have the experience of doing it with pack goats on invitation from Clay Zimmerman (http://www.highuintapackgoats.com/). On that trip, my adopted daughter from Guatemala, Mahana, became the first Guatemalan we know of to traverse the Wilderness. In the spontaneous narration there are a couple of mistakes, like once saying “crossroad,” rather than “cross trail;” saying “Amethyst Creek,” rather than “Ostler Creek,” “Lost Lake,” rather than “Shadow Lake,” and the big one, stating King’s Peak in one place as being 15,528 ft. high rather than 13,528 ft. There might be a few more, but also the coordination between narration, and photographs is sometimes off a second or two. One day I might redo the program and hope for better luck. In the meantime, enjoy the beautiful High Uintas Wilderness like maybe you’ve never seen before. 1000 Mile Backpack in the Uintas link: http://vimeo.com/10558175 #03-2015 “THE GRANDADDIES” all the lakes in the basin are shown. #02-2015 High Uinta Mts.–ACCLIMATIZE ON MT. 04/12/2019 -- I am working hard to overcome my chronic bronchitis and be in shape for one key backpack in 2019--a much greater test of my resolve. There will be an update on my website for 2019 efforts. Thanks to all and hope to see you on the trail. Your High Uinta “TRAIL BUDDY,” Cordell M. Andersen
